member.name: M:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Architecture.Notifications.TransactionNotificationService.ProcessPossibleRemodeledUpdates(Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Contracts.Data.Architecture.Notifications.NotificationUpdate,Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Architecture.BaseClasses.NamedObjectBase)
member.summary: The method was introduced to handle the Remodeled properties from a newer version if the SPI.Net with a version of the Proxy that doesn't know about the new model properties.
member.param: The main notification update packet that might contain unknown property updates
The Server object associated with the update
member.remarks: This is intended to be processed from older Proxies (older than the service it is connecting to) to maintain the same update processing it has been used to. For instance, SIPLACE Pro Proxy 3.1 calls ComponentShape.TravelProfilePickupLower=2 (where it was 1) on the SIPLACE Pro Service 3.2. That call will be converted to a call to the ComponentShape.TravelProfileTypePickupLower=Standard for instance. There is no update on the SPI.Net for the property TravelProfilePickupLower. So, the SPI Service will generate a new RemodeledNotificationUpdatePacket object that contains the update (fake) for the old TravelProfilePickupLower with a NewValue=2, OldValue=1. This method then will be called and the local SPI Proxy ComponentShape object will process the update for the old property (TravelProfilePickupLower) correctly

member.summary: The method was introduced to handle the Remodeled properties from a newer version if the SPI.Net with a version of the Proxy that doesn't know about the new model properties. It is called by the ProcessPossibleXXX method which checks if there are any remodeled packets to process. If so, then this method will call the actual object with the prepared updates that are converted from remodeled packets to standard update packets
member.param: The Main (traditional) update packet that contains the remodeled packets as well

So, the SPI Service will generate a new RemodeledNotificationUpdatePacket object that contains the update (fake) for the old TravelProfilePickupLower with a NewValue=2, OldValue=1. This method then will be called and the local SPI Proxy ComponentShape object will process the update for the old property (TravelProfilePickupLower) correctly

Minimum value is 1 minute, maximum value is 30 minutes. Can be configured in the app.config under "Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxies.ReliableChannel.KeepAliveChannelsEveryMinutes"

member.name: M:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Architecture.Objects.IdentityList.GetFolders(System.String)
member.summary: Get a List of Folders based upon a formatted parameter string
member.param: Formatted parameter string depicting the query
member.remarks: The return values of this method may change from SIPLACE Pro version to version. Please use Session.GetFoldersFromCache to use a consistent return behavior. strParms Format is "ft:path" where ot = FolderType name of object (example : "Board") path = the complete path name of Folder (example : "Temp\Folder1")
member.example: example1: "Board:Temp\Folder1" gets the Board Folder with name "Folder1" which is in Folder "Temp" example2: "Board:RootFolder1" gets the Board Folder with name "RootFolder1" which is in the root Folder example3: "Board:*" gets all the Board Folders that are in the root (excluding subfolders, excluding root folders) example4: "Board:Temp\*" gets all the Board Folders in the Temp Folder (excluding subfolders) example5: "*" gets all Folders of all types (including the root folders and all subfolders!)

member.param: Formatted parameter string depicting the query
member.remarks: strParms Format is "ot:path" where ot = ObjectType name of object (example : "Board") path = the complete path name of object (example : "Temp\Board1")
member.example: example1: "Board:Temp\Board1" gets the Identity of the Board1 example2: "Board:BoardRoot1" gets the Identity of the BoardRoot1 example3: "Board:*" gets all the Identities for all Boards example4: "Board:Temp\*" gets all the Identities for all Boards under the Temp Folder example5: "*" gets all the Identities

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Architecture.Objects.Session.ObjectCacheSynchronizeTimerEnabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the loaded objects should be automatically synchronized with the adapter, so that the adapter object cache contains also the same server objects as the proxy. This does NOT mean the object tree of the loaded objects in the proxy, but this affects only the server object cache on the SPI Adapter side. Client side cache synchronization is on by default and can be deactivated by TransactionNotificationService.Disable() and enabled by Enable() methods. Alternatively, you can use the UpdateBlockingScope to block proxy updates temporarily. Automatic synchronization happens on a timer thread. The timer can be configured using the ObjectCacheSynchronizeFrequency property. When using the automatic synchronization, it may happen that client calls take longer than expected since the timer driven synchronization is running on the adapter at that moment and the client call blocks until synchronization has finished.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Architecture.Objects.Session.ObjectCacheSynchronizeFrequency
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating the frequency how often the loaded objects should be automatically synchronized with the adapter, so that the adapter object cache contains also the same server objects as the proxy (only used in case ObjectCacheSynchronizeTimerEnabled property is set to true).

member.summary: Performs a Copy of a Server object (given the Identity). This copies only the identities specified and NO other Server Objects within the hierarchy. All identities in identitiesToCopy must be of the same object type and the destinationFolder must match this object type.
member.param: The source objects that should be copied. All objects must be of the same server object type.

The prefix for the newly copied objects. This property is only used in case an object with the same name already exists in the destination folder. Can also be left null or empty. In case it is null or empty, a unique number is appended.
member.returns: The newly created Identities for the copied objects.

member.summary: Performs a Copy of a Server object (given the Identity). This copies all the data and other Server Objects within the hierarchy as specified in the dictionaryCopyDeepControl parameter. All identities in identitiesToCopy must be of the same object type and the destinationFolder must match this object type.
member.param: The source objects that should be copied. All objects must be of the same server object type.

The prefix for the newly copied objects. This property is only used in case an object with the same name already exists in the destination folder. Can also be left null or empty. In case it is null or empty, a unique number is appended.

Specifies how the copy operation should copy referenced object types. If they should be copied, an entry in the dictionary must be supplied. The folder (value of the dictionary) is optional. If the value in the dictionary is null, the copied object will be put into the same folder as the original object. If an object type is not present in the dictionary, the copy operation will not copy these object types. If an object type is missing in the hierarchy, it's sub-objects are not copied either. Example: You copy a PlacementList and the dictionaryCopyDeepControl only contains an entry for ComponentShape, but not Component. This leads to ComponentShapes not being copied!
member.returns: The newly created Identities for the copied objects.

member.name: M:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Architecture.Objects.Session.GetFolders(System.String)
member.summary: Get a List of Folders based upon a formatted parameter string
member.param: Formatted parameter string depicting the query
member.remarks: The return values of this method may change from SIPLACE Pro version to version. Please use GetFoldersFromCache to use a consistent return behavior. strParms Format is "ft:path" where ot = FolderType name of object (example : "Board") path = the complete path name of Folder (example : "Temp\Folder1")
member.example: example1: "Board:Temp\Folder1" gets the Board Folder with name "Folder1" which is in Folder "Temp" example2: "Board:RootFolder1" gets the Board Folder with name "RootFolder1" which is in the root Folder example3: "Board:*" gets all the Board Folders that are in the root (excluding sub-folders, excluding root folders) example4: "Board:Temp\*" gets all the Board Folders in the Temp Folder (excluding sub-folders) example5: "*" gets all Folders of all types (including the root folders and all sub-folders!)

member.name: M:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Architecture.Objects.Session.GetFoldersFromCache(System.String)
member.summary: Get a List of Folders based upon a formatted parameter string
member.param: Formatted parameter string depicting the query
member.remarks: strParms Format is "ft:path" where ot = FolderType name of object (example : "Board") path = the complete path name of Folder (example : "Temp\Folder1")
member.example: example1: "Board:Temp\Folder1" gets the Board Folder with name "Folder1" which is in Folder "Temp" example2: "Board:RootFolder1" gets the Board Folder with name "RootFolder1" which is in the root Folder example3: "Board:*" gets all the Board Folders (including sub-folders, excluding root folders) example4: "Board:Temp\*" gets all the Board Folders in the Temp Folder (excluding sub-folders) example5: "*" gets all Folders of all types (including the root folders and all sub-folders!) example6: "Board:Temp\*\*" gets all the Board Folders in the Temp Folder (including sub-folders) example7: "Board:.\*" gets all the Board Folders the root Folder (excluding sub-folders)

member.example: example1: "Board:Temp\Board1" gets the Identity of the Board1 example2: "Board:BoardRoot1" gets the Identity of the BoardRoot1 example3: "Board:*" gets all the Identities for all Boards (including sub-folders) example4: "Board:Temp\*" gets all the Identities for all Boards in the Temp Folder (excluding sub-folders) example5: "*" gets all the Identities Added in SIPLACE Pro versions > 15.0: example6: "Board:Temp\*\*" gets all the Identities for all Boards in the Temp Folder (including sub-folders) example7: "Board:.\*" gets all the Identities for all Boards in the root Folder (excluding sub-folders)

member.example: example1: "Board:Temp\Board1" gets the Identity of the Board1 example2: "Board:BoardRoot1" gets the Identity of the BoardRoot1 example3: "Board:*" gets all the Identities for all Boards (including sub-folders) example4: "Board:Temp\*" gets all the Identities for all Boards in the Temp Folder (excluding sub-folders) example5: "*" gets all the Identities Added in OIB 5.3: example6: "Board:Temp\*\*" gets all the Identities for all Boards in the Temp Folder (including sub-folders) example7: "Board:.\*" gets all the Identities for all Boards in the root Folder (excluding sub-folders)

member.name: M:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Architecture.Objects.Session.StartBulkTransaction(Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Architecture.Objects.BulkTransactionType,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Start a Bulk transaction for high performance data input into the system. Should be used carefully since many trade-offs are made to gain performance.
member.param: The type of bulk data to import.
Whether the bulk objects will be used after the import.
member.remarks: Internal function not to be used by OIB client applications. Objects being changed by bulk transactions are not updated in the SPI cache of other clients. Once an object is changed within a bulk transaction other clients MUST need to call Reload(). Use the ClientUpdateService.ObjectRequiresReloadEvent event to receive updates from other clients that have imported data on your currently cached objects. BulkTransactionType.CadWizard - Deprecated enum, not implemented in latest versions. Sane functionality as the LineComputerImport. BulkTransactionType.LineComputerImport - Bulk Import Board/PlacementList ComponentPlacements. Optimized to import large number of ComponentPlacements fast. BulkTransactionType.Optimization - Deprecated enum, not implemented in latest versions. Bulk Import Recipe optimization data. Optimized to import large number of ComponentPlacements fast. BulkTransactionType.GerberData - Deprecated enum, not implemented in latest versions. Was bulk importing Gerber data but Gerber data removed some years ago.

member.name: M:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Architecture.Objects.Session.StartTransaction
member.summary: Start a Transaction which needs to be followed by a Commit or Rollback. You must ensure you catch any exceptions and call a Rollback() otherwise the state of any future transactions will be never committed.

member.name: M:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Architecture.Objects.Session.ThrowErrorOnModelAccessViolations(System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: This will set global flags used for illegal access of properties/methods that aren't supported for all versions. So for example, calling BoardSide.InterferingEdgeZ is only valid in SIPLACE Pro V5.1 installation and above. If client code calls the get_InterferingEdgeZ on a BoardSide object against a SIPLACE Pro V4.1 installation, the code can either throw an exception or return the default value and continue on. The reverse is also applicable where a Model Method/Property has been removed in future versions. In this case the Contract still contains the Method/Property but newer versions don't support it at runtime. So these flags will set the intended behavior for these situations as well.
member.remarks: Once these flags are set, they will be active the lifetime of the Session object.
member.param: True:throws an error for calling get_Property of unsupported version. False: Returns the default value. Default:False
True:throws an error for calling set_Property of unsupported version. False: Just returns. Default:False
True:throws an error for calling any Method of unsupported version. False: Returns a default value. Default:True

True:throws an error for calling any Add, Remove, Clear on a Collection of unsupported version. False: Treats the Collection as a Temporary (non-persistable) Collection with allowed Adds, Remove, Clears, etc. Default:False

The reverse is also applicable where a Model Method/Property has been removed in future versions. In this case the Contract still contains the Method/Property but newer versions don't support it at runtime. So these flags will set the intended behavior for these situations as well.
member.remarks: Once these flags are set, they will be active the lifetime of the Session object.
member.param: True:throws an error for calling get_Property of unsupported version. False: Returns the default value. Default:False

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Interfaces.IMatrixTrayFeederType
member.summary: Interface of the matrix tray feeder type object, a static object that stores read-only matrix tray Feeder attributes. Matrix tray feeders present Components housed in two stacked containers (towers) with 40 levels (carriers) or 30 and 40 (MTC2), each of which contains one or more trays that house components in their receptacles.The most necessary components typically are positioned on the bottom levels.The total tray changing time used by Optimization is CarrierYTime plus the vertical moving time, which is calculated from the vertical Carrier distance and the MTC's moving time function t(z), which in turn is based on CarrierZTimexx() and ChangeTimeOneLevel().

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Interfaces.ISetup
member.summary: Interface of the setup object, a user-defined server object. SIPLACE Pro works with two different Setups: In the context of a Job, a 'Start' Setup is the object from which an optimizer reads Line configuration information about equipment available to produce a Board or boards based on the stations in the line. In the context of a Recipe, a 'Result' Setup is the object to which an optimizer writes optimized equipment configuration information to produce a board based on stations in the line.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Interfaces.IStation
member.summary: Interface of the station object, a server object that represents a placement machine positioned in a Line. Two important properties are IPAddress and SW_Version: While the use of the first property is obvious, the second requires the correct version of software currently on the placement machine station computer.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Interfaces.ITrayFeederType
member.summary: Interface of the tray feeder type object, a static object that stores read-only dimensions and other information unique to a particular tray Feeder type that can be accessed when configuring a desired feeder in a Setup.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Interfaces.ITrayReserve
member.summary: Given a carrier index and component, assign the component to the tray reserve. If there is no tray reserve, create one and then assign the component to the tray reserve----------------------------------------This interface implements TrayReserve, a user-defined non-server object, which defines physical and functional characteristics of trays used with waffle pack changers and other tray feeders,Notes: A reserve is a 'pocket' or area where a component is picked up. A TrayReserve encompasses all receptacles on a tray Feeder (and, therefore, can be visualized as the tray itself). OffsetX and OffsetY properties position the tray on a Carrier

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AtxCommon.IdlePressure
member.summary: This parameter allows the user to Enable or Disable the Idle Paste Pressure parameter.When enabled: (And when the ProFlow unit is idle.) The solenoid valve is switched to allow the software controlled air regulator(SCAR) to control the piston(s). The piston(s) remain at 0 Bar idle paste pressure. The user can opt to apply more crosshead/paste pressure by overriding the default value and setting an idle paste pressure between 0 and 4 Bar.When disabled: The solenoid is switched bypassing SCAR; the piston(s) are retracted.Additional Information This parameter applies to all ProFlow types. The crosshead piston or the paste pistons are controlled in the same manner.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AtxCommon.SystemPressure
member.summary: Sets the amount print pressure (downward force) applied onto the screen by the ProFlow Unit.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AtxCommon.TransferHeadSize
member.summary: ProFlow ATx Transfer Head Types. Contains the set of widths for the Head Size

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AtxCommon.GridSpeedCoefficient
member.summary: Grid Speed Coefficient

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AtxCommon.PastePressureDelay
member.summary: Used to define the additional time required to enable the specified value of paste pressure to be attained prior to commencing a print stroke.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AtxCommon.PressureDecayInterval
member.summary: This parameter sets the time period where the paste pressure is released and the paste is allowed to relax. It aims to prevent paste leakage from the transfer chamber at the end of the print stroke and before board separation takes place. Additional Information: During this interval, system pressure remains on, to maintain the contact with the screen, and is released at the end of the interval.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.CadWizardFormat
member.summary: CadWizard format object.A server object to create a customized parsing application, which enables you to convert CAD data in particular file formats (e.g., .txt or .cad) into component placement data.Currently, the ASCII centroid data and CAD import wizard imports only the following information: Reference Designator, Component, Package Form, X, Y, Angle, and Side. There is additional information that can be extracted from the ASCII centroid data and CAD file that is useful during New Product Introduction, NPI, and programming. Such info includes CAD Shape and CAD description. By including these two pieces of data the user will have a better chance in determining if a part is a fiducial, surface mount component, through hole component, or drawing attribute.In ASCII centroid and CAD file: CAD shape and CAD descriptionIn BOM file: component description

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.BoardDIB
member.summary: BoardDIB, containing links to board bitmaps and providing a means to depict and position associated fiducials.The BoardDIB is the object one would use to overlay a Bitmap picture of the Board against the real placement list to see if they match.
Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: Blob containing bitmap. A blob is a large binary file for storing different image types. Use this type of link to maintain a live connection to a particular blob object.
Binary stream of parameters/ extended data. For internal use only.
The Shear value in the X direction. This will present the BoardDIB (picture) with a sheared effect in the drawing engine (or equivalent).
The Shear value in the Y direction. This will present the BoardDIB (picture) with a sheared effect in the drawing engine (or equivalent).
The Scale value in the X direction. This will present the BoardDIB (picture) with this scaling factor (shrink or enlarge the picture) in the drawing engine (or equivalent).
The Scale value in the Y direction. This will present the BoardDIB (picture) with this scaling factor (shrink or enlarge the picture) in the drawing engine (or equivalent).
The Image Offset value in the X direction. This will present the BoardDIB (picture) with an offset from the Board in the drawing engine (or equivalent).
The Image Offset value in the Y direction. This will present the BoardDIB (picture) with an offset from the Board in the drawing engine (or equivalent).
The property stores the original file name (full path) for history purposes only. It is not used for any business rules, etc.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.BoardElement.OffsetX
member.summary: Property that determines the X offset of a board within the board element collection. This property takes the board offset mode into account: In case the offset mode is set to explicit_offset the value is equal to ExplicitOffsetX. It is read- and writeable, where writing directly manipulates the explicit offset property. In case the mode is set to automatic_offset_X, this property is readonly, and reflects the offset of the board by adding the board length (or width, depending from the orientation) of its predecessor to the offset of its predecessor in the board element collection vector. Any write access in this mode will produce an exception.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.BoardElement.OffsetY
member.summary: Property that determines the Y offset of a board within the board element collection. This property takes the board offset mode into account: In case the offset mode is set to explicit_offset the value is equal to ExplicitOffsetY. It is read- and writeable, where writing directly manipulates the explicit offset property. In case the mode is set to automatic_offset_X, this property is readonly, and the value will be the values of its predecessor in the board element collection vector. Any write access in this mode will produce an exception.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.BoardElement.OffsetZ
member.summary: Property that determines the Z offset of a board within the board element collection. This property takes the board offset mode into account: In case the offset mode is set to explicit_offset the value is equal to ExplicitOffsetZ. It is read- and writeable, where writing directly manipulates the explicit offset property. In case the mode is set to automatic_offset_X, this property is readonly, and the value will be the values of its predecessor in the board element collection vector. Any write access in this mode will produce an exception.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.BoardElement.XDimension

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.FiducialList
member.summary: FiducialList object, functioning as a wrapper to the FiducialPlacement Collection, which works with existing local/panel fiducials.It references all associated FiducialPlacements appearing on a BoardSide and, if present, Panels on the BoardSide. There can be two FiducialList objects associated with a BoardSide, one references local, panel, and board fiducials (via BoardSide's FiducialList object property) and the other references inkspots (via BoardSide's InkspotList object property). Like a PlacementList, a FiducialList has no physical geometry of its own.

member.name: M:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.FiducialList.#ctor(System.Nullable{System.Double},System.Nullable{System.Double},System.Nullable{System.Double})
member.summary: Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: To be hidden. Sometimes a board and its corresponding screen image do not align exactly because they are not the exact same dimensions, a result of screen stretch or low quality boards. AlignWeight helps align normal-sized board and screen images in 2 fiducial mode by working with corresponding board/screen fiducial locations where the best alignment occurs.Note: Two fiducial mode refers to the process during which a printer's vision system examines 2 board fiducials in conjunction with their 2 corresponding screen fiducials. Set alignment weighting at 100% where the best alignment occurs at fiducial 1. Set alignment weighting at 0% where the best alignment occurs at fiducial 2. Use in between percentages when best alignment occurs between the fiducials.

Sometimes a board and its corresponding screen image do not align exactly because they are not the exact same dimensions, a result of screen stretch or low quality boards. AlignWeightX helps align large board and screen images along the board's x axis in 3 fiducial mode by working with corresponding board/screen locations where the best alignment occurs.Note: In 3 fiducial mode, the printer vision system examines 3 board fiducials in conjunction with their 3 corresponding screen fiducials. 0%X 0%Y indicates best alignment occurs at the board's bottom left corner. 50%X 50%Y indicates best alignment occurs at the center of the board.

Sometimes a board and its corresponding screen image do not align exactly because they are not the exact same dimensions, a result of screen stretch or low quality boards. AlignWeightY helps align large board and screen images along the board's y axis in 3 fiducial mode by working with corresponding board/screen locations where the best alignment occurs.Note: In 3 fiducial mode, the printer vision system examines 3 board fiducials in conjunction with their 3 corresponding screen fiducials. 0%X 0%Y indicates best alignment occurs at the board's bottom left corner. 50%X 50%Y indicates best alignment occurs at the center of the board.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.GenericLineDevice.OffsetZeroPointX
member.summary: Offset X vector from object's origin to zero point of its current position. For example, SIPLACE Pro assigns the center of a waffle pack tray to be its origin for drawing and positioning purposes. The ZeroPointX Offset is the vector from that origin to the x coordinate to the lower-left corner of the actual waffle pack tray (or tray reserve). This property is user-defined for IBoardside, IPanel, IReceptacle, and ITrayReserveType only (mm's).

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.GenericLineDevice.OffsetZeroPointY
member.summary: Offset Y vector from object's origin to 0 point of current position. For example, SIPLACE Pro assigns the center of a waffle pack tray to be its origin for drawing and positioning purposes. The ZeroPointY Offset is the vector from that origin to the X coordinate to the lower-left corner of the actual waffle pack tray (or tray reserve). This property is user-defined for IBoardside, IPanel, IReceptacle, and ITrayReserveType only (mm's).

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.GenericLineDevice.OffsetZeroPointZ
member.summary: Offset X vector from object's origin to 0 point of current position. For example, SIPLACE Pro assigns the center of a waffle pack tray to be its origin for drawing and positioning purposes. The ZeroPointZ Offset is the vector from that origin to the Z coordinate to the lower-left corner of the actual waffle pack tray (or tray reserve). This property is user-defined for Receptacle only.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.GerberFile
member.summary: Represents an imported gerber file
Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: Binary stream of parameters/ extended data. For internal use only.
The property stores the original file name (full path) for history purposes only. It is not used for any business rules, etc.
The Offset value in the X direction.
The Image Offset value in the Y direction.
The Scale value in percent. This will present the Gerber image with this scaling factor (shrink or enlarge the image) in the drawing engine (or equivalent).
Contains the angle of rotation relative to the board side.
Coordinate system, distinguishes an object's particular type of coordinate system (e.g., how the gerber data is mirrored).
Specify whether the visualization of the Gerber data should consider the coordinate system of he board side to which it belongs.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.LeadBallCircle
member.summary: A user-defined non-server object, which representsa circular or 'leadless' lead (representing chip carriers, flat contacts, etc.) for creating a package form (e.g., component shape). Unlike other leads, LeadBallCircle enables you to set offsets.

member.name: M:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.LeadBallCircle.#ctor(System.Nullable{System.Drawing.Color},System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Nullable{System.Double},System.Nullable{System.Double},System.Nullable{System.Double},System.Nullable{System.Double},System.Nullable{System.Boolean})

Object diameter as expressed in mm's.

Tolerances affect the vision system search area. Typically you would adjust these properties only when dealing with leads of unusual dimensions. Excessively small tolerances result in unusually high rejection rates while larger tolerances can result in skewing and/or the placing of less than acceptable components.
Offset X vector relative to the parent object in mm's. The x direction is parallel to the direction the board moves through the printer/placement machine.
Offset Y vector relative to the parent object in mm's. The Y direction is perpendicular to the direction the board moves through the printer/placement machine.
Specifies if lead is brighter than background (contrast)

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.NozzleAcceleration
member.summary: Each nozzle is rated to work with a certain range of components. At times, however, the size and weight of a particular component may require nozzle acceleration to be reduced to prevent dropping or damaging components.In such cases, a NozzleAcceleration object with customized 'reduced acceleration' values should be associated with the ComponentShape through the NozzleCameraRel object's NozzleAccelerationCollection.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.NozzleCrossSection
member.summary: A system and user-defined non-server object (to work with custom or user-defined NozzleTypes), which contains data describing the area nozzles use to handle components. This data is useful so users can visually determine in SIPLACE Pro Desk whether a nozzle is a good fit for a specified component shape. Below are two different nozzle cross sections, the first with two separations and the second with none:
Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: Cross section shape, Body shape assigned to nozzle cross section. (0 -- rectangle, 1 -- ellipse/circle, 2 -- user defined)
Inner width of a nozzle cross section. Default: 0.0For rectangle, it stands for the width of the inner contour;for ellipse/circle, it stands for the 1st diameter of the inner contour

Inner length of a nozzle cross section. Default: 0.0For rectangle, it stands for the length of the inner contour;for ellipse/circle, it stands for the 2nd diameter of the inner contour.(if it is circle, the two diameters are the same)
Outer width of a nozzle cross section. Default: 0.0For rectangle, it stands for the width of the outer contour;for ellipse/circle, it stands for the 1st diameter of the outer contour

Outer length of a nozzle cross section. Default: 0.0For rectangle, it stands for the length of the outer contour;for ellipse/circle, it stands for the 2nd diameter of the outer contour.(if it's circle, the two diameters are the same)
Number of separations in the nozzle suction area. Below are two different nozzle cross sections, the first with two separations and the second with none. Default: 2

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.PatternFeature
member.summary: Pattern feature is a non lead feature on the component shape, which can be used for measuring,compatible to SIPLACE VIsion 5.4 ff (SW 710 ff). A Pattern Feature is modeled by one or more edge points (or ?edgels?). The term ?edgel? is a blend of ?edge? and ?pixel? and means a position which is defined as the edge of something. In the context used here, each edgel represents a piece of an edge of the feature. In total, the feature, which can have arbitrary shape, is defined by a set of edgels (or edgel pattern)

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.DipHandlingInfo
member.summary: Handling information concerning the dipping process of the Component Shape
Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: Time in ms how long the Component has to remain in the Dip-Medium
Determine if the coverage of component shape by the dip flux medium should be checked by the vision system. This requires SIPLACE Vision V35.
Flux thickness specifies, at which level the component has to be dipped. The parameter is used by the optimizer, to bind a component to a specific Dipping unit, which is configured with this level.
The dip flux material, which has to be used when the component is processed.
Defines if custom settings for the creed distance while dipping are used.

In the placement process, the value determines the distance, which the placement head will creep before the component is expected to touch the surface of the dipping unit. The attribute takes only affect on stations running station software 709 and higher. On other stations this will be ignored.
Can be used to reduce the speed of the axis when dipping while moving down towards the dipping surface.
Can be used to reduce the speed of the axis when dipping while moving up from the dipping surface
Switches the dipping force to low.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.PolarityMark
member.summary: A Polarity Mark is a reference point on a component that helps ensure the component will be placed at the appropriate placement angle. A polarity mark physically appears on a component as a small circular mark positioned on a particular corner (or a 'cut off' corner or edge).However, the angle at which the component is placed always relates to the assigned package form and board. In other words, the polarity mark is not used by the machine to determine the orientation of the component. PolarityMark objects are intended only to assist users in identifying the orientation of the component in a graphical user interface.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.TableType.OffsetZeroPointX
member.summary: Offset X vector from object's origin to zero point of its current position. For example, SIPLACE Pro assigns the center of a waffle pack tray to be its origin for drawing and positioning purposes. The ZeroPointX Offset is the vector from that origin to the x coordinate to the lower-left corner of the actual waffle pack tray (or tray reserve). This property is user-defined for IBoardside, IPanel, IReceptacle, and ITrayReserveType only (mm's).

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.TableType.OffsetZeroPointY
member.summary: Offset Y vector from object's origin to 0 point of current position. For example, SIPLACE Pro assigns the center of a waffle pack tray to be its origin for drawing and positioning purposes. The ZeroPointY Offset is the vector from that origin to the X coordinate to the lower-left corner of the actual waffle pack tray (or tray reserve). This property is user-defined for IBoardside, IPanel, IReceptacle, and ITrayReserveType only (mm's).

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.TableType.OffsetZeroPointZ

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.FiducialLink.FiducialTypeNumber
member.summary: Every fiducial for placement purposes (e.g., local, board, and panel) consists of a given fiducial type. Each fiducial type has an 'MC Number,' which is required to work with the Station Computer. As a result, every Fiducial Link object has its FiducialTypeNumber property set to the 'MC Number' value of the corresponding Fiducial Type.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.FiducialLink.FiducialFunction
member.summary: Translates the Fiducial's Local/Panel flags and indicates a classification of fiducial. Can indicate one OR MORE of the following values (combined by logical-or): GlobalInkspot, Inkspot, PCBFiducial, LocalFiducial

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.GridBoard
member.summary: A GridBoard is an optimized board structure for highly regular panel structures with equally distributed component placements. Used in e.g. wafer level fan out process. A grid board consists from grid panels which itself are from a grid panel type. The grid panel type consists from grid packages. Each grid package has a grid package type. The grid package type contains the coupler to the placement list and is named by a char. A package map (two dimensional array of chars) defines how different packages are arranged on the grid panel type.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.Barcode
member.summary: Barcode object. The constraints on the barcode can be represented with the filter. For instance, certain bit has to be set to certain value. A barcode is a printed code that identifies printed circuit boards, components, and table tracks to SIPLACE Pro. Barcodes appearing on component reels and table tracks enable users to verify they are matching the correct components with the correct tracks. Barcodes also help identify screens when working with printers.

member.name: M:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.Barcode.#ctor(System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: A filter is a pattern through which data is passed. Use the Filter property to use portions of existing barcodes. The filter may only contain any combination of 1' and 0's that is equal to the length of the BarcodeString property.

User can assign a barcode range to a Board. Thus, all individual boards which have a barcode from this range are manufactured according to the specifications for the board to which this range is assigned
Assign the barcode string and set the filter accordingly

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.BoardSide
member.summary: BoardSide object, use it to access the top and/or bottom side of a board during the placement process.
Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: Offset X vector from object's origin to zero point of its current position (mm). For example, SIPLACE Pro assigns the center of a waffle pack tray to be its origin for drawing and positioning purposes. The ZeroPointX Offset is the vector from that origin to the x coordinate to the lower-left corner of the actual waffle pack tray (or tray reserve).

Offset Y vector from object's origin to 0 point of current position (mm). For example, SIPLACE Pro assigns the center of a waffle pack tray to be its origin for drawing and positioning purposes. The ZeroPointY Offset is the vector from that origin to the X coordinate to the lower-left corner of the actual waffle pack tray (or tray reserve).

True if the object will be skipped during placement process. Default: False. Note: Using an inkspot means the placement machine makes the decision to place/not place at runtime depending on whether it finds the inkspot or not.
Changes an object's color in SIPLACE Pro Desk. (RGB)
Coordinate system, distinguishes an object's particular type of coordinate system (e.g., how the bottomside of a Board is mirrored).

Thickness of the solder paste on the pads in mm's (for Coplanarity purposes).Note: Coplanarity is an option that checks gull-wing components for bent leads while a pad is conductive portion of a board typically used for the connection/attachment of components via leads. Bent leads may result in a faulty/non-existent connection between a component lead and a pad given the specified thickness of solder paste.
Sets the distance from the front edge of the board to the print area.Note: With ProFlow fitted, the minimum value is 0mm.
Sets the distance from the rear edge of the board to the print area.Note: With ProFlow fitted, the minimum value is 0mm.
Stores a reference to a global inkspot via its name.

If a user overlays a bitmap on a board in order to position components on the board, the board side needs to be transparent; otherwise, the bitmap would be obscured. True if the board side is Transparent. Default = False.
Dictates how board will oriented during placement operations.
Stores a reference to a PCB detection inkspot via its name
An additional interfering edge in Z direction on the boardside, which has to taken into account, when the placement head moves over the board in order to prevent from a collision.
If True, the optimizer chooses initial (locator) fiducials from all fiducials on the board, regardless if these are belonging to panels, that don't have a component placement position.
The support pin list defines a set of support pin positions that are used to produce this board side.
Enables the measuring of the warpage on the station.
Defines a maximum value of the board warpage.

Switches the component shortage tracking on and off. Shortage tracking is a line feature, which assures that the amount of all components of a board are available in the current setup of the line. Otherwise it is prevented that the production of the board will be started.
Switches if a board side is used in a Product Group. The name of the product group is set in the attribute ProductGroupName
The attribute determines the product group to which the board side is belonging. All board sides which have the identical value are belonging to the same product group.
The guid links two or more board sides together, which are produced. Used by LED Pairing.
Determines the position correction method the station will use to correct the component positions while placing.
The sequence order of the production in case 2 board sides are produced.
Selects the board side for PCB counting
Determines the weight class of the board.
Defines the period in seconds after which time the fiducial has to be measured again by the station. 0 means never.
Determines if the board barcode label for this board side is located on the opposite side and has to be read by a barcode reader from below.
Name string of the board side. Required for backward-compatibility with the Line Computer.

A Placement list contains all the necessary component placement data to place components on a board (via board sides and panels). Use this type of link to maintain a live connection to a placement list.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.Component
member.summary: Component object (Server Obj).The Component object stores pick-up information unique to a particular type of electronic/mechanical device to be mounted on a board. Both the Component and ComponentShape objects contain several identical object properties (e.g., DefaultFeederType): If these identical object properties are assigned values for the component's associated componentshape, then assigning values for these component object properties is optional unless they differ. If you assign different values to identical object properties of a particular component and componentshape, then the values assigned to the component object will override those of the component shape.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.Component.RejectFeeder
member.summary: Enables IComponent and IComponentShape to work with a reject feeder. Reject feeders function as a storage area for components that fail vision system inspections can be transferred for safe keeping, as a opposed to the reject bin, where the components may be damaged. Once a component is moved to a reject feeder, users can collect them and return them to the manufacturer. You cannot pick up components from a reject feeder. Default: false

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.ComponentPackage
member.summary: A server object that enables a user to edit default feeder settings to suit a specific component (to ensure a good seal between a nozzle and a component). The values that you set in this object overwrite existing FeederOffset values.Notes: This object is especially helpful, for instance, if you have a 10 different components that can be loaded on the same feeder: Instead of adjusting feeder settings for each component, you can reference this object for all ten. This object is not depicted in this help file's Object Model Reference section due to its standalone nature. In the SIPLACE Pro Desk's user interface, a Name field appears in the Component Package Properties dialog. The Component Package 's Identity appears here (There is no Component Package Name property).

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.ComponentPlacement
member.summary: ComponentPlacement object, storing placement information unique to a particular component. Before assigning placement data to this object's properties (e.g., OffsetX, OffsetY, etc.) you should first create a Board, PlacementList, and Component. After creating a ComponentPlacement object, you need to add it to the ComponentPlacementCollection. Typically, you will assign component placements in the process of importing a CAD file.
Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: Offset Y vector relative to the parent object in mm's. The Y direction is perpendicular to the direction the board moves through the printer/placement machine.

Offset X vector relative to the parent object in mm's. The x direction is parallel to the direction the board moves through the printer/placement machine.Default: 0.0 mm. Max/min values vary by object (e.g., IPanel's Max = 480.0 Min = -480.0 whereas IGroup's Max = 100.0 Min = -100.0)

The Component object stores pick-up information unique to a particular type of electronic/mechanical device to be mounted on a board. Use this type of link to maintain a live connection to a component.
Angle as expressed in radians for offset purposes. Different objects have different max/min values. Default: 0.0 (rad)
Optional color value of a component placement. Currently not used in SIPLACE Pro Desk.

Levels enable you to control the order in which a particular component will be placed relative to other components for efficiency purposes. Taller components, for instance, should be placed after shorter components to eliminate unnecessary lateral movements by the head. Default: 0Note: The higher the level, the later the component will be placed relative to other components.
Contains the name of the component shape in the BOM (bill of materials) file at the time of import.
Contains comments about an imported component shape (which help to recognize fiducial data and to clean up unneeded data in an imported CAD file) from a BOM (bill of materials) file.
Contains comments about an imported component from a CAD file. Max: 50 chars.
Specifies the level of transparency. Is evaluated if Transparent property is set to true.
Determine if a offset of a placement position has to be taught on the station. This attribute is used in conjunction with the PlacementOffset object.
Contains additional offset information, which is relevant for the feature teaching of placement positions. In case the reference is null the position hadn't been taught.
Selects a placement position to be glued.
Determines of the component top side needs to be optically centered. For this a special processes and a LED Offset Sensor have to be used. Supported by station software version 707 ff.

True if the object will be skipped during placement process. Default: False. Note: Using an inkspot means the placement machine makes the decision to place/not place at runtime depending on whether it finds the inkspot or not.

True ensures that only this component will be placed on a Panel or a Board. Default: False. (It determines if this placement has to be reworked. If there is at least one placement anywhere on the board with this flag set, then for the whole board only placements with this flag set shall be processed.)
Specifies the string that identifies this object to the user

member.summary: Z axis movement profile for picking up a specific component.Note: While this feature was specifically introduced for 0201 components, all component shapes have configurable travel profiles in order introduce special handling capability. 'Crawl' refers to moving at a slower rate than normal.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.ComponentShape.Force
member.summary: Force to place a component on a board. The placement force depends on the following parameters: material and size of the component, nozzle material, and composition (consistency) of the adhesive or solder paste used to place the component.
member.remarks: [DefaultValue(2.0)] [RangeValueAttribute(0.0, 100.0)] In case PlacementForceSetting is set to Standard this property will return 2.0 N. In case PlacementForceSetting is set to VeryLowForce this property will return 0.5 N. In case the special placement process is set to touch less or spring or touchless smt, the force will always be 0.0 N

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.ComponentShape.Thickness
member.summary: The actual height of a component. Notes: Component body height and lead height contribute to ComponentShape Thickness; however, Thickness is not necessarily the sum of lead length and body height as leads are often mid-mounted on a body. Thickness value is best obtained from a data sheet. Component length and width is handled via the DIPF object. If a component's height exceeds 4mm, the component sensor camera can only check for presence of the component.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.CameraType
member.summary: Camera type object, a static object that contains read-only information unique to each placement station camera. Note: A camera helps center components on a board by producing the raw data that enables the vision system to generate the correct offset information. Since camera type is based on head type, different heads require different cameras. A pick-and-place head, for instance, requires a higher resolution camera than a revolving head. In order to verify that a component can be scanned by a camera (component is inside the camera focus range) more geometric information about the camera are needed: on the camera side, we need to know the camera built-in height and its focus range or its focus height (depends on the camera type) on the nozzle side, we need to know the nozzle length and the component height (and its height tolerance)

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.BodyHCyl
member.summary: BodyHCyl : horizontal cylinder typeA user-defined non-server object, which stores the characteristics of a horizontal cylinder component body. After creating a DIPF object and linking it to a ComponentShape object, get this object via DIPF's GetBody method. A body's offset and its pickup location, where the nozzle makes contact with the component, are independent--even though in most cases the center of the body will be where the nozzle makes contact. Body offset is not used by the vision system.

Both TopSide and BottomSide object properties access the BoardSide object.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.Board.AllowReducedFiducialMeasurementSteps
member.summary: Allows the optimizer to reduced the amount of measured fiducials from 3 to 2 in case one is not possible to be measured.Normally the optimizer measures 3 fiducials for each panel if these are defined.In case it is not possible to measure one of these (e.g. travel range restrictions), the optimizer will automatically measure only the two reachable ones.This behavior can lead to inaccurate component placements.So a new attribute is defined at the board, which allows the user to switch off this behavior. What means at least 3 fiducials have to be measured (if defined).
member.exception: This property is only fully supported in SIPLACE Pro Version(s) [V10.0 and above] Any attempt to call the set_AllowReducedFiducialMeasurementSteps will result in an exception otherwise. However, calling get_AllowReducedFiducialMeasurementSteps will return the default value if applicable without an exception raised. See Session.ThrowErrorOnModelAccessViolations for settings on version behavior.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.Board.EnforcedFiducialCount
member.summary: Determines the minimum number of fiducials, which have to measured for position correction. Default is undefined, which means three are measured if available but two are also allowed.Normally the optimizer measures 3 fiducials for each panel if these are defined.In case it is not possible to measure one of these (e.g. travel range restrictions), the optimizer will automatically measure only the two reachable ones.This behavior can lead to inaccurate component placements.This attribute allows the user to switch off this behavior. What means at least 3 or 4 fiducials have to be measured (if defined).
member.exception: This property is only fully supported in SIPLACE Pro Version(s) [V11.1 and above] Any attempt to call the set_EnforcedFiducialCount will result in an exception otherwise. However, calling get_EnforcedFiducialCount will return the default value if applicable without an exception raised. See Session.ThrowErrorOnModelAccessViolations for settings on version behavior.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AttachableHeadType.FunctionPrinciple
member.summary: Read-only. Describes how components will be picked up and placed. HP_COLLECT_N_PLACE indicates that a revolver head will pick up numerous components and then place them, while HP_PICK_N_PLACE indicates that a pick-and-place head will pick-up and place one component at a time. Used for optimization.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AttachableHeadType.ID
member.summary: Read-only. Identifies type equipment for download purposes. For internal use.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AttachableHeadType.Radius
member.summary: Read-only. Turn radius of the head in which every segment and associated component must fit. Used by Siemens optimizer.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AttachableHeadType.MaxDiagonal
member.summary: Read-only. The maximum length of a component measured diagonally across its body. Used to dictate maximum component size per specific head used so its rotational range is not exceeded (which could result in collisions with other components).

member.summary: Links to a list of available nozzles.

member.summary: Read-only link to associated INozzleChangerTypes in the IAllowedResourceTypeCollection.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AttachableHeadType.NormalParkPosZ
member.summary: Collision border of a head in z direction , in case the head moves without components.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AttachableHeadType.ParkPosMin1SegmentZ
member.summary: Collision border of a head in z direction, in case the head moves without components and has let one segment empty (this is used on the CP head of F machines to gain a higher placement height of the corresponding IC head)

member.summary: For Future use. Intended to describe the allowed collision diameters along the z-Axis.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AttachableHeadType.StaticSegments
member.summary: All segments of the head type.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AttachableHeadType.MaxNozzleAcceleration

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AttachableHeadType.MaximumPlacementForce
member.summary: The maximum force, which can be applied by the placement head when placing a component on the board.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.AttachableHeadType.PrecisionCapabilities
member.summary: BitSet value from t_PrecisionClass, which determines the precision capabilities of the head type. e.g. used for CP20 M head, to describe the enhanced accuracy of the head type.

member.summary: Maximum moment of inertia which the head can handle with the DP axis.0.0 means no limitation.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.StaticStationConveyorSystem
member.summary: Implements the attributes belonging to one lane of a conveyor system type that is assembled in a station type.Is reference able by dynamic objects.

Retrieve the position of the fixed rail of a conveyor lane, which is depending from the selected wideness, the orientation, the conveyor mode and the placement mode.In case the method returns true the out value dFixedRailPosition is a valid position. In case false is returned the selected operation settings are not supported, by this conveyor system and the out value is invalid.
member.returns: See Summary for details. This method will return a type bool with default value of false
member.remarks: For use with all SIPLACE Pro versions.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.StaticAttachableHead.PCBCameraOffsetY
member.summary: Y offset of the PCB camera to the origin of the head. Built-in position of the PCB Camera.The station S25HM2 has a modified travel range in order to support 0201 placement phase 2. The extended travel range allows for the camera to use the tape pocket for feeder position recognition. This achieves an improved pickup rate.A new implementation (also for HS50/55) will check, if feeder pockets can be send to the station instead of feeder drillings. LineControl does this by checking: Stationtravelrange - PCBCameraOffsetY )= Pocket position.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.PlacementList
member.summary: PlacementList (Server Obj): a server object that contains all the necessary component coordinate data to place Components on a Board (via BoardSides and Panels). Typically, the PlacementList object is populated with CAD data. When working with the PlacementList object, you can also omit components or ensure that a particular component is the only one placed (for testing purposes). Fiducials can be managed similarly. A PlacementList has no physical geometry of its own.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.LeadWraparound
member.summary: A user-defined non-server object, which stores the characteristics of a particular component lead that does not protrude from the body of the component. Also referred to as a 'leadless' lead or flat contact.
Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: Illumination values between -1 (dull) and 100 (reflective) to be used with a placement machine vision system. Default = -1.

Permissible length tolerance of a component's leads permitted by the vision system (in mm's). Excessively small tolerances result in unusually high rejection rates while larger tolerances can result in skewing.

Permissible width tolerance of a component's leads permitted by the vision system (in mm's). Excessively small tolerances result in unusually high rejection rates while larger tolerances can result in skewing.
Overall width of a lead, which connects a component to a pad, in mm's.
Overall length of a lead in mm's.

LeadGullwing and LeadWrapAround may have a notch or a hole that should be considered by image processing. In this case, the 'Notch Width' attribute can be used to specify the approximate width of the notch.
Specifies if lead is brighter than background (contrast). Default direction of the contrast, true means bright.

member.summary: Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.

Permissible width tolerance of a component's leads permitted by the vision system (in mm's). Excessively small tolerances result in unusually high rejection rates while larger tolerances can result in skewing.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.LeadGullwing
member.summary: A user-defined non-server object, which stores the characteristics of a particular component lead loosely shaped like a Gull's wing
Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: Illumination values between -1 (dull) and 100 (reflective) to be used with a placement machine vision system. Default = -1.

Permissible length tolerance of a component's leads permitted by the vision system (in mm's). Excessively small tolerances result in unusually high rejection rates while larger tolerances can result in skewing.

Permissible width tolerance of a component's leads permitted by the vision system (in mm's). Excessively small tolerances result in unusually high rejection rates while larger tolerances can result in skewing.
Overall length of a lead in mm's.
Overall width of a lead, which connects a component to a pad, in mm's.
Lead width in mm's that contacts the circuit board when placed. This value will typically be equal to lead width.
Lead length in mm's that contacts the circuit board when placed. This value will always be less than total lead length.

LeadGullwing and LeadWrapAround may have a notch or a hole that should be considered by image processing. In this case, the 'Notch Width' attribute can be used to specify the approximate width of the notch.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.Group
member.summary: A group of Leads.This object specifies types of leads a DIPF object can possess. A group must consist of leads of the same type, all having the same distance (pitch) with respect to one another. All the leads in one group are to be found along one side of the shape. The origin of a leadgroup is in the center of the object. Lead groups cannot be assigned names.
Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: Number of leads in the group
Spacing of the leads (mm), based on the center of the lead.
Angle as expressed in radians for offset purposes. Default: 0.0
Group Offset X (mm). Offset X vector relative to the parent object in mm's. The x direction is parallel to the direction the board moves through the printer/placement machine.
Group Offset Y (mm), Offset Y vector relative to the parent object in mm's. The Y direction is perpendicular to the direction the board moves through the printer/placement machine.
The amount that the pitch can vary by before a error is reported. For example if a lead is bent slightly it will be fine if the distance it is off is less than the pitch limit error.
The tolerance value for the colinearity check.

Determines if the pitch limit can be different in X and Y direction. Can be used in conjunction with THT pins in case the PCB has slot holes. If true the PitchLimitError and the PitchLimitErrorY will be the same. If false the PitchLimitError contains the X limit and the PitchLimitErrorY contains the Y limit.
The amount that the pitch in Y direction can vary by before a error is reported. For example if a lead is bent slightly it will be fine if the distance it is off is less than the pitch limit error.
Additional information used for Special Position Evaluation
Vector from the lower edge of the component shape to the level where the leads of the group are located.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.RecipeElement
member.summary: RecipeElement object. Before optimizing a job, you can specify the importance of a particular recipe so that it affects the end result of the optimization process. Assign higher priorities to recipes with larger numbers of boards. Used for the RecipeCollection in the Job.

member.name: M:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.RecipeElement.#ctor(Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.Recipe,System.Nullable{System.Int32})
member.summary: Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: Specifies the importance of a particular Recipe in a Job so that the optimization process produces an algorithm especially efficient for the production of the Recipe's board (as opposed to other boards in the Job if the Job contains multiple Recipes.). In general, you assign higher priorities to Recipes with the largest lot sizes (or quantities) of boards in the Job. Default: 0.Note: The FabMaster optimizer does not use the Priority property.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.DIPF
member.summary: DIPF : object of Device Independent Package Form.An object that contains information describing a component's physical dimensions (derived from leads and bodies) in addition to some component handling information. This object specifies one of four shapes a ComponentShape object can possess via the BodyType object property. ComponentShapes must always be linked to DIPF objects to be used by the system.You can link a single Component Shape to different DIPFs throughout the system.BodyType is read only: Use NewBodyType or the Body property to set BodyType and GetBody or the Body property to return a body object (e.g., BodyRect).To calculate DIPF length/width, store lead length(s)/width(s) and body length/width in DIPF Length/Width. SizeTolZ is not implemented at this time.

member.summary: Get next computed name for lead groups
member.param: Whether to incorporate SIPLACE Vision or not.

Total length of DIPF (component body + leads) in mm's. Typically, you should set this value using the sum of body and lead lengths. Note: Length equates to the X dimension, which aligns with the long side of the nozzle).

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.FeederOffset
member.summary: FeederOffset object: corrective offset from nominal pickup position in a feeder's reserve to the center of the component shape. Use this object to work with components that are not positioned in the center of a feeder's reserve. This offset affects where SIPLACE Pro will look for a component in a feeder's reserve. An incorrect feeder offset could result in a poor seal between a nozzle and a component. Note: Different feeder reserve types have different feeder offsets and origins. For instance, the linear feeder's origin is at the top center of the reserve, whereas tape and tray feeder reserve origins are located in the center.
Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: Acceptable angle deviation (in degrees) a component in a reserve is permitted by the vision system. Values set in ComponentPackage's ToleranceAngle property will overwrite values set in this property.Note: Only PackAngleTolerance and ToleranceAngle (ComponentPackage) work with degrees rather than radians.

Use this property to adjust the X coordinate from which a component will be picked up in a feeder (X is the direction of board travel). Values set in ComponentPackage's Offset X property will overwrite values set those set in this property.

Use this property to adjust the Y coordinate from which a component will be picked up in a feeder (Y is perpendicular to the direction of board travel). Values set in ComponentPackage's Offset Y property will overwrite values set those set in this property.

Use this property to adjust the Z coordinate from which a component will be picked up in a feeder. By setting this property to 1.0, for example, ensures a component will be picked up 1 mm above its nominal position. Values set in ComponentPackage's Offset Z property will overwrite values set those set in this property.
No of components on the tape after which the tape will be cut
Offset Vector X of optional fiducial measured from Pickup point.
Offset Vector Y of optional fiducial measured from Pickup point.
Use TypeRef object property to maintain a connection to a live 'type' object (e.g., StationType for Station).
This time describes the time needed to switch from another component sort to this one. (e.g. level change.) This time is introduced to enable the user to adjust the timing for the wafer feeder.
Contains the pick up position value of a tape feeder, in case it had been changed from the calculated default value. 0 represents an unchanged value.
Offset Vector X of optional barcode fiducial measured from pickup point.
Offset Vector Y of optional barcode fiducial measured from pickup point.
Reference to the optional barcode fiducial type.
Index of the handling data set which should be used in case of a Bulk Feeder X.
Specifies if the waiting time value is customized (always true for linear reserves, optionally on tape reserves)
member.remarks: [DefaultValue(1)] [RangeValueAttribute(1, 1000)] Setter automatically adjusts: Waiting time (based on the current pitch)
member.param: Pitch (spacing between successive components). The pitch values defined in the IFeederOffset of a component overrides the one which is defined in the IFeederOffset of a ComponentShape.
member.remarks: [DefaultValue(0)] [RangeValueAttribute( 0, 999 )] Setter automatically adjusts: Waiting time (based on the XFeederTravelProfile)
member.param: Maximum acceptable deviation (in mm) a component in a reserve is permitted by the vision system along the x axis (direction of board travel). Values set in ComponentPackage's ToleranceX property will overwrite values set in this property.

Maximum acceptable deviation (in mm) a component in a reserve is permitted by the vision system along the Y axis (perpendicular to the direction of board travel). Values set in ComponentPackage's ToleranceY property will overwrite values set in this property.
Angle as expressed in radians to adjust for the component's angle in a feeder. Note: Values set in this property will be overwritten by values set in ComponentPackage's Angle property.
Time (in ms) the Head is waiting for the component to be available for pick up. Values set in ComponentPackage's WaitTime property will overwrite values set those set in this property.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.Fiducial
member.summary: Fiducial object.Maybe user or system-defined non-server Fiducial objects. Despite the many uses for fiducials on a board, SIPLACE Pro uses Fiducial objects in association with component pick-up operations for calibration purposes only. Refer to FiducialPlacement and FiducialType objects for more information about fiducial objects involved in component placement operations (associated with BoardSide, Panel).
Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: Use TypeRef object property to maintain a connection to a live 'type' object.
Offset X vector relative to the parent object in mm's. The x direction is parallel to the direction the board moves through the printer/placement machine.
Offset Y vector relative to the parent object in mm's. The Y direction is perpendicular to the direction the board moves through the printer/placement machine.on DEK, OffsetX and OffsetY -- [0, 510]
Angle as expressed in radians for offset purposes.
True if the object will be skipped during placement process. Default: False
Value will only be evaluated if FiducialPlacement is of type fiducial (not inkspot) and if the ToleranceMode is either Limited or AllowMultipleMeasurement.

Determines how the station will measure a fiducial: Default 'FieldOfView': the station will perform one measurement and use the field of view of the PCB camera to detect the fiducial. In case there are other interfering structures near to the fiducial on the PCB it is possible to reduce the tolerance by setting the ToleranceMode to 'Limited'. In case position of fiducial is very inaccurate, the mode can be switched to 'Allow multiple measurement'. This will trigger a station running station software version 707 or higher to perform several measurements with the PCB camera to cover a larger area.

member.summary: Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.FiducialPlacement
member.summary: FiducialPlacement object, storing local, board, panel, inkspot, and screen fiducial positional information unique to a particular fiducial; it also provides links to fiducial type objects, which store the physical characteristics of a fiducial. Typically, you will work with fiducial placements when importing CAD data.
Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: The reference designator (unique id) of the associated component for local Fiducial Placements. Note: This property is called 'Placement Position Reference' in the Desk's user interface.
If True, determines if a fiducial placement is assigned to a Panel fiducial. Default: False.

True if the object will be skipped during placement process. Default: False. Note: Using an inkspot means the placement machine makes the decision to place/not place at runtime depending on whether it finds the inkspot or not.
True indicates if a fiducial position is assigned to a local fiducial. Default: False.
Angle as expressed in radians for offset purposes. Default: 0.0
True indicates that fiducial is for printing purposes only. Default: False
Value will only be evaluated if FiducialPlacement is of type fiducial (not inkspot) and if the ToleranceMode is either Limited or AllowMultipleMeasurement.

Explicitly limit the set of fiducials on a board, that are measured in the first step, in order to determine the board position in the placement area. This might be necessary in case there are fiducial positions existing on a board, that might be not measurable during the production phase. e.g. Fiducials that are covered by components or panels that are not present in the current PCB (work piece holders).
Extended for updating all the Fiducials in a relationship (Panel Matrix)
Determines if the exact position of the fiducial needs to be taught by the station software.
A reference designator is a user-defined unique string (usually obtained from a placement list) necessary to work with specific instances of the ComponentPlacement/FiducialPlacement object.

member.name: P:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.FiducialPlacement.ToleranceMode
member.summary: Determines how the station will measure a fiducial: Default 'FieldOfView': the station will perform one measurement and use the field of view of the PCB camera to detect the fiducial. In case there are other interfering structures near to the fiducial on the PCB it is possible to reduce the tolerance by setting the ToleranceMode to 'Limited'. In case position of fiducial is very inaccurate, the mode can be switched to 'Allow multiple measurement'. This will trigger a station running station software version 707 or higher to perform several measurements with the PCB camera to cover a larger area.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.FiducialType
member.summary: The server object of FiducialType. Both system-defined fiducial types (static objects) associated with feeder fiducials and user-defined fiducial types (server objects) associated with local, board, panel, and screen fiducials as well as inkspots. FiducialTypes contain information about a fiducial's physical characteristics. This object enables you to create or choose from existing fiducial types. To work with fiducials on panels and boards, you will typically create them. Choose from system-created fiducials (e.g., 250 and 251) when working with a setup. Fiducial 250 is the track-teaching tool while 251 is the feeder fiducial.

member.name: T:Asm.As.Oib.SiplacePro.Proxy.Business.Objects.MatrixTrayFeeder
member.summary: Matrix of tray feeder objects.A user-defined non-server object, which presents components housed in two stacked containers (towers) with 40 levels (carriers), each of which contains one or more trays that house components in their receptacles. A matrix tray feeder is comparable to a Waffle Pack Changer, which possesses only 28 levels.
Overloaded Constructor to pass in initialize values. Pass in null for the Nullable parameters to use the default value.
member.param: Acceleration in Z direction (up and down). Default: 0.0 mm
Acceleration in Y direction (perpendicular to conveyor). Default: 0.0 mm
Allow the optimizer to setup more than one tray on a level of a tower.
Where first track feeder will begin at (0 for empty).
If True, the current feeder will not be re-positioned during subsequent optimizations. Default: False.
Offset X vector relative to the parent object in mm's. The x direction is parallel to the direction the board moves through the printer/placement machine.
Offset Y vector relative to the parent object in mm's. The Y direction is perpendicular to the direction the board moves through the printer/placement machine.
Offset Z vector relative to the parent object.
